name: Cutting alcohol for smell

lead: Some people stop or reduce drinking hoping their sweat and breath smell cleaner. It is usually one step among several grooming changes.

Body odour mainly arises when skin bacteria break down gland secretions, and general references list food, drink, gut microbiome and genetics among the influences. Believers suggest alcohol adds to this. No study found tests abstinence for this purpose.

paras: People cut back or stop drinking, often alongside better sleep, hydration and hygiene habits. Reports usually describe noticing changes after days to weeks.

Cutting alcohol is not associated with a documented odour-related harm in the sources reviewed. People who drink heavily are generally advised by clinicians to seek medical guidance before stopping suddenly.

angle.text: People in grooming circles cut alcohol in the belief that sweat, breath and body odour become less noticeable and the natural scent cleaner. The idea rests on personal reports, with no dedicated studies behind it.

lead: Cutting alcohol for smell is a lifestyle practice in which people reduce or stop drinking alcohol in the belief that it will make their sweat, breath or general body odour less noticeable.[1] It is discussed in appearance and grooming circles as part of a wider approach to smelling clean.

Body odour is generally attributed to bacterial activity on skin gland secretions, and encyclopedic sources list food, drink, gut microbiome and genetics among the influences on it.[1] No published trial found in the sources reviewed here has tested alcohol abstinence specifically as a way to change body odour, so the practice rests largely on personal reports.
infobox: Less noticeable sweat or breath odour

paras: Practitioners report cutting back on alcohol as one change among several aimed at body odour, alongside hygiene, clothing and diet changes. The practice is informal and has no standard protocol.

Wikipedia describes the major source of body odour as bacteria acting on apocrine and other skin gland secretions, with Corynebacterium and Staphylococcus species producing odorous compounds.[1] The same article names food, drink, gut microbiome and genetics as factors, and notes that a variant in the ABCC11 gene strongly alters odour in some populations.[1] The article does not discuss alcohol specifically.

lore.intro: Community discussion of alcohol and smell is mostly anecdotal and is not tied to any source reviewed for this entry.

claims.claim: Drinking alcohol makes sweat smell worse, so quitting improves body odour.
